answers.label: An empty folder: a new service or monorepo

suggestions.title: Read how the platform fits together
suggestions.text: Ten minutes on the pieces, what stays yours and how a request travels through them.

suggestions.title: Bootstrap the solution with the CLI
suggestions.text: dotnet tool install --global Anarchy.Toolkit.Automation.Build.Cli, then anarchy-toolkit bootstrap. You get the standard folder-layered solution, Anarchy build, Makefile and first applications. Preferences are optional; opt in to saving selected values.

suggestions.title: Follow the greenfield walkthrough
suggestions.text: Layout choices, applications, mock server and the pull-request gate, step by step.

answers.label: An existing solution that keeps shipping

suggestions.title: Read how the platform fits together
suggestions.text: Ten minutes on the pieces, what stays yours and how a request travels through them.

suggestions.title: Follow the adoption walkthrough
suggestions.text: Small, deployable pull requests in a proven order: repository files, build, layering, tests, mock server, settings, modules, startup, telemetry.

suggestions.title: Choose how the layering check maps projects
suggestions.text: Pick one mode for the whole solution: folder (recommended) when projects sit in layer folders such as src/Library/Core, prefix when they are named Core.*, Infrastructure.*. The folder baseline needs no config file; pass explicit arguments or optionally save overrides in .anarchy-toolkit.json. Map application folders instead of moving files, and add check_layering once it passes locally.

suggestions.title: Sync the repository files first
suggestions.text: anarchy-toolkit boilerplate diff .gitignore .editorconfig, then install them into managed blocks and run make lint_fix in a formatting-only commit.

answers.label: An application that only needs one capability

suggestions.title: Add packages one at a time
suggestions.text: dotnet add package Anarchy.Toolkit.<Package>, then apply its module as its README describes. No build or layout changes needed.

questions.text: How should your projects map to layers?
questions.help: One mode for the whole solution. Optional overrides live in .anarchy-toolkit.json; without them, folder mode uses src/Library and standard app folders. Layers: Core, Infrastructure, Configuration, Hosting, Web, with Automation for build tooling on top.

answers.label: By folder, several applications sharing a library (recommended)

suggestions.title: Use folder layering with a shared Library
suggestions.text: src/Library/Core, Infrastructure, Configuration and optional Web, plus src/Api, src/Jobs and src/Ui applications. This is the default baseline; save custom library and application mappings only when needed.

suggestions.title: Bootstrap with the single-app layout
suggestions.text: The bootstrap wizard asks one application or several before layering mode. For non-interactive setup, use --layout single-app: layer projects live directly under src, libraryRoot is src, and one application folder maps to Web (API/UI) or Hosting (job). Choose its folder with --application-folder.

suggestions.title: Use prefix layering
suggestions.text: Fully supported and used by the toolkit itself; suited to separately packaged projects. Pass prefix mode to the operation or optionally save { "layering": { "mode": "prefix" } } in .anarchy-toolkit.json.

suggestions.title: Validate settings on start
suggestions.text: One AppSettings class with DataAnnotations, registered with ModuleAppSettingsBase.

suggestions.title: Log and measure through AppTelemetry
suggestions.text: Register telemetry once (ModuleLibConfiguration does it, or services.AddCoreTelemetry()) and inject AppTelemetry. Logs go to your Microsoft logging providers, metrics to the standard .NET meter that OpenTelemetry exports with OTLP. Serilog is optional.

answers.label: Correlation IDs across requests, workers and messages

suggestions.title: Propagate correlation IDs without a logging dependency
suggestions.text: UseCorrelationId() for HTTP, CorrelationContext.BeginScope for workers, and BeginCorrelationScope on mapped SQS messages put the IDs into ILogger scopes and activity tags, so any provider and OpenTelemetry carry them.

suggestions.title: Use the persistence layer
suggestions.text: Unit of work, retry policies, reader/writer repositories and health reports for PostgreSQL, MySQL or Oracle. Install the provider package for your database; it brings Infrastructure.Persistence.Db.

answers.label: AWS messaging (SNS/SQS; the only supplied transport today)

suggestions.title: Publish and consume with AWS
suggestions.text: AWS SNS/SQS is currently the only supplied transport, with modules tested against a local AWS emulator. Core.Messaging.Abstractions is the broker-neutral extension point for implementing another broker.

suggestions.title: Run workers with health
suggestions.text: MonitoredWorkerBase for loops, HealthCheckBase for dependency checks.

suggestions.title: Add the mock server
suggestions.text: JSON expectations in MockServer's format, assertions on what was received, no Docker.

questions.text: Does your pipeline call build or make targets that must keep their names?

answers.label: Yes, and the pipeline is hard to change

suggestions.title: Add Anarchy automation next to your targets
suggestions.text: Install the Makefile and scripts with --append-existing, keep your targets in your own .mk files listed in MAKE_EXTRA_TARGETS, with their names unchanged.

answers.label: Yes, and our build also deploys

suggestions.title: Keep release separate from build
suggestions.text: Keep the deploying build in a separate release host next to build/, and use Anarchy automation for development and the pull-request gate.

answers.label: No, we can change it freely

suggestions.title: Add Anarchy automation
suggestions.text: A build host with IStandardBuild, then make pull_request as the pipeline's single command.

questions.text: Which test stack do you use today?

suggestions.title: Use the testing kits
suggestions.text: TestCaseBase, fixtures and TestTelemetry, which captures logs and metrics in memory, for your tests.

answers.label: NUnit, MSTest, xUnit v2 or something else

suggestions.title: Use your test framework, or start on xUnit v3
suggestions.text: The build runs any test project; only the Testing.* kits assume xUnit v3 on Microsoft.Testing.Platform. New test projects can follow the xUnit v3 recipe.

questions.text: How are your test projects named?

suggestions.title: Declare your test project names
suggestions.text: TestKindAliases in .fallout/parameters.json, e.g. ["EndToEnd=Acceptance"]. Keep unit tests free of I/O: packing runs them.

questions.text: How do your tests stand in for HTTP upstreams?

suggestions.title: Add the toolkit mock server
suggestions.text: JSON expectations in MockServer's format, a check with ShouldAllHaveBeenMatched that fails the run on unmocked calls, and a pinned port.

answers.label: WireMock, hand-written fakes or real services

suggestions.title: Consider the mock server later
suggestions.text: Keep what works. The toolkit mock server is optional; it pays off when Docker or flaky upstreams slow the pipeline down.

answers.label: Add* extensions that read their own configuration

suggestions.title: Validate settings, then write one module per adapter
suggestions.text: Add AppSettings, then one module per adapter, smallest first, each tested in isolation.

suggestions.title: Group registrations into one module per concern
suggestions.text: One module per adapter, without changing behaviour, then build the host on the toolkit's startup.

answers.label: We'd rather keep it as it is

suggestions.title: Call the extensions directly
suggestions.text: Every toolkit module wraps an Add* extension or plain registrations you can call yourself.

questions.text: Will your applications call other HTTP services?

suggestions.title: Add a mock server project from day one
suggestions.text: A project ending in MockServer, expectations per upstream, IMockServerBuild, and ShouldAllHaveBeenMatched in the tests.

questions.text: Which kinds of applications do you run?

suggestions.title: Build APIs on Web
suggestions.text: anarchy-toolkit scaffold api <Name>; Input/Output DTOs at the boundary.

suggestions.title: Serve GraphQL
suggestions.text: GraphQL.NET with GraphiQL on the Web pipeline.

suggestions.title: Build jobs on Hosting
suggestions.text: anarchy-toolkit scaffold job <Name>; JobEntryPointBase with the same modules and settings as your APIs.

suggestions.title: Run workers on MonitoredWorkerBase
suggestions.text: One iteration per call; cancellation, failure logging, heartbeats and health endpoints included.

suggestions.title: Build UIs on Web.Ui
suggestions.text: anarchy-toolkit scaffold ui <Name>; Blazor with cookie-session login.

questions.text: Which relational database do you use?

suggestions.title: Use the PostgreSQL provider
suggestions.text: ModulePostgres, reader/writer repositories and a container-backed test kit.

suggestions.title: Use the MySQL provider
suggestions.text: ModuleMysql on MySqlConnector. If you use MySql.Data today, the driver differs: test it against your database first.

suggestions.title: Use the Oracle provider
suggestions.text: ModuleOracle, retry policy and a test kit for an oracle-free container.

questions.text: Do you run local dependencies (databases, brokers, emulators) in Docker?

suggestions.title: Manage containers from the build
suggestions.text: IDockerBuild with docker/docker-compose.yml: make start, stop, destroy and container waits.

questions.text: Does your organization have its own logging, metrics, auth, feeds or deployment?

answers.label: Logging or metrics backend (Datadog, New Relic, Grafana, ...)

suggestions.title: Send telemetry to your backend with OTLP
suggestions.text: Add an OpenTelemetry OTLP exporter listening to the toolkit meter and configure the endpoint, API key and temporality with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* variables. Package the setup in one ModuleTelemetryBase kept in a company folder and reuse it in every solution.

suggestions.title: Configure Datadog or New Relic
suggestions.text: Both ingest OTLP: no vendor package and no vendor API in your code, only exporter configuration. Notable events are structured logs with a stable EventId that a provider or exporter can map to vendor events.

suggestions.title: Keep Serilog as a logging provider
suggestions.text: AddSerilogTelemetry registers your configured logger as one more Microsoft logging provider, so toolkit logs reach your sinks and instrumentation code stays the same.

suggestions.title: Add your auth handlers in your own module
suggestions.text: A DelegatingHandler for outbound tokens; mock-server expectations and unsigned tokens for tests.

answers.label: A deployment tool the toolkit doesn't ship

suggestions.title: Keep a separate release build
suggestions.text: Anarchy automation builds packages and container images; deploying is yours, in a release host next to build/.

questions.text: How much of the toolkit's way of working do you want?

answers.label: All of it: we want the decisions made for us

suggestions.title: Adopt the conventions and the layering check
suggestions.text: Add ILayeringBuild to the pull-request gate and follow every convention, including naming, UseCases and Aggregates; read the values behind them.

answers.label: Gradually, as we see the benefit

suggestions.title: Adopt conventions one at a time
suggestions.text: Start with Testing and Dependency Injection, which the build and packages benefit from most, then Code Organization and Naming; record each deviation in an ADR.

answers.label: Packages and build only, not the conventions

suggestions.title: Skip the conventions, knowingly
suggestions.text: Every convention page ends with how to opt out and what you lose. Leave ILayeringBuild out of the build.
